docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This guide outlines steps for using the browser version of LinkedIn: a networking platform that allows you to create a professional profile, connect with colleagues, search for jobs, and build industry skills.

To follow this guide, sign up for a LinkedIn account or log into an existing one.

docs.title: LinkedIn for job applications
docs.text:
New and experienced users alike can take advantage of LinkedIn's professional development tools to streamline the job search and application process:

  • Set up your profile
  • Add job preferences
  • Search for jobs
  • Apply for a job
  • Track application progress

docs.title: LinkedIn Premium Career
docs.text:
With LinkedIn Premium Career, a paid subscription service, you can stand out to recruiters and colleagues with advanced hiring analytics, tailored LinkedIn Learning options, and more:

  • View analytics for a job posting
  • Mark a job as your Top Choice
  • See who has viewed your profile
  • Learn with LinkedIn Learning
  • Activate Premium Perks

See Standard vs Premium Career to learn more about the difference between the free and paid LinkedIn experiences.

Note

LinkedIn Premium offers certain features in beta mode to a select group of LinkedIn Premium subscribers. Therefore, certain features in this guide may be unavailable to all users until future public rollout.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
You can customize your job preference to receive emails, internal notifications, and refined search results about the jobs that are best suited for you. Preferences can include job titles, location, start dates, employment types, and more.

  1. On your profile page, click the Open to button under your headline.
  2. Click Finding a new job from the dropdown menu.
  3. Fill in the required fields to specify your job preferences.
  4. Click Save.

docs.title: Find recommended jobs
docs.text:
Job recommendations will be sent to you via email and through your internal LinkedIn notifications.

You can also find recommended jobs by clicking the Jobs icon in the top navigation bar. Jobs that fit your preferences best will be listed first.

Note

Premium users can view additional details about other applicants, job criteria, and recruiter feedback. To learn more about Premium analytics, see View analytics for a job posting.

docs.title: Related tasks
docs.text: • Search for jobs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Every LinkedIn job listing offers one of two ways to apply: external applications and Easy Apply.

External applications typically direct you to a company's talent acquisition site or a SaaS platform such as Workday.

Easy Apply is LinkedIn's internal application submission system, allowing you to apply for a job with your LinkedIn profile (and without leaving the LinkedIn site) rather than creating an external candidate account.

docs.title: Apply using external applications
docs.text:
1. After finding a job listing whose description matches your preferences, click Apply. A new tab will be opened in your browser.

  2. Complete the application according to the talent acquisition site's requirements.

  3. (Optional) After completing the application, return to the LinkedIn posting and select Yes in the following prompt:

    By selecting Yes, you can track your application progress in LinkedIn from the job tracker. You can access applied jobs by returning to the Jobs landing page and clicking Job tracker.

docs.title: Apply with Easy Apply
docs.text:
1. Click Easy Apply under a job listing.

  2. Fill in any required fields. These often include contact information, a CV, and a cover letter, but exact requirements vary by listing.

  3. Click Review once you have completed the application to look over your responses.
  4. Click Submit application to send your application to the recruiter.

With Easy Apply, your application is automatically added to the Job tracker.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: LinkedIn allows you to strategically search for jobs according to title, required skillsets, pay, location, company type, and more. You can use its search and explore features to find jobs that align with your job preferences.

docs.title: Search by job title, skill, or company
docs.text:
1. Click on the Jobs icon in the top navigation bar.

  2. Enter your desired job title, skillset, or company name into the search bar. You can also specify a location (city, state, or country) to refine your search.

  3. Scan search results for jobs that interest you.

  4. (Optional) Click Save to save a job listing for later. You can access saved jobs by returning to the Jobs landing page and clicking Job tracker.

docs.title: Explore with job collections
docs.text:
LinkedIn also allows you to explore jobs by pre-curated job collections, such as Unicorns, Easy Apply, and Series AB (see Reference: Job collections to learn more about individual job collection categories).

  1. From the Jobs landing page, scroll down to reach the Explore with job collections section.
  2. Click Show all.
  3. Select a job collection to filter job listings.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A professional profile on LinkedIn acts as your digital CV. You can showcase your experiences, educations, skills, and more to impress recruiters and find the jobs that are the best fits for you.

docs.title: Add an intro
docs.text:
A LinkedIn intro contains the first information that recruiters and other LinkedIn users will see when previewing or visiting your profile.

Edit your intro by completing the following steps:

docs.title: 1. Access your profile
docs.text:
1. To access your profile, click your profile picture on the top right of the navigation bar.

  2. From the dropdown, select View profile.

docs.title: 2. Edit intro details
docs.text:
1. Click the pencil icon to the right of your profile picture to open the editing panel, then enter your info.

    Although not all fields are required, filling out more information increases the reach of your professional profile. Learn more about intro fields and their usage.

  2. Click Save after entering your info.

docs.title: Add experiences and other qualifications to your profile
docs.text:
1. On your profile page, scroll down to the experience type you want to update (for example, Experience, Education, or Skills).
  2. Click the plus icon in that section.
  3. Fill any required fields with your information.
  4. Click Save.

Tip

To reorder any entries in a section, click the pencil icon in that section, then click the reorder icon to the left of the plus icon.

Reorder your entries in the popup, then exit to save.

docs.title: Share your profile
docs.text:
After polishing your profile, you can share it as a URL for recruiters and colleagues to access.

On your profile page, copy the link under Public profile & URL. Paste the link into your resume, online portfolio, or anywhere you want to promote your LinkedIn profile.

docs.title: Customize your profile's URL
docs.text:
You can customize your URL's slug (in other words, the end of the URL) to create a more readable or representative link to share with the public.

URL customization example

DefaultCustomized

www.linkedin.com/in/mmorrison1810

www.linkedin.com/in/margaret-morrison

Follow these steps to customize your URL slug:

  1. Click the pencil icon next to Public profile & URL (see image above). A new tab opens in your browser.
  2. Under Edit your custom URL, click the pencil icon.
  3. Enter a custom URL slug. The custom slug must contain 3-100 letters or numbers, and it cannot use spaces, symbols, or special characters.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: You can keep track of the jobs you applied to within the job tracker, which allows you to update application statuses and archive old job listings.

docs.title: View jobs you applied to
docs.text: From the Jobs landing page, click Job tracker. Select a filter (Saved, In Progress, Applied, Interview, or Archived) to view your jobs.

docs.title: Update application status
docs.text:
For each job in the job tracker, you can simply respond to the prompts to update your status.

Alternatively, you can click the ellipsis icon (...) to quickly archive or change the stage of your application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
LinkedIn Premium Career is a paid subscription service that enhances the free LinkedIn experience with advanced tools for job seekers, sales professionals, and business growth. Key features include InMail messages to contact anyone, insight into who viewed your profile, unlimited browsing, and AI-powered learning resources.

Start a free trial of LinkedIn Premium Career to use the features included in this guide.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: LinkedIn Premium subscribers are able to redeem Premium Perks, which include free trials to applications that help you achieve your personal and professional goals.

docs.title: Redeem Premium Perks
docs.text:
1. Click Me in the top navigation bar.

  2. From the dropdown and under Account, select Premium features.

  3. Scroll down to the Redeem Premium Perks section.

  4. Select the perk you want to redeem.

  5. Complete any required sign-up process to access your free trial for the selected application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: LinkedIn Learning provides support for professional development and certifications through AI coaching and online courses. You can use LinkedIn Learning to prepare for interviews, gain qualifications for jobs that interest you, and display certificates on your profile.

docs.title: Take online courses to develop career skills
docs.text:
1. To access LinkedIn Learning, click the Learning icon at the end of the top navigation bar.

    This will open the Learning Career Hub.

  2. In the search bar, enter the role, skill, or industry you want to take a course on.

    The search will retrieve the courses that best fit your desired outcomes.

  3. Select a course that aligns with your goals.

  4. Complete all lectures, readings, and quizzes to earn a certificate for that course.

docs.title: Practice for interviews with AI-powered role play
docs.text:
AI-powered coaching allows you to role play work conversations or prepare for your next interview. Coaching can be completed through audio/speech features (microphone required) or typing.

  1. From the Learning home page under the Apply section, select AI Role Play.

  2. In the AI role play prompt, enter the scenario or conversation you want to practice. For example: "I want to practice negotiating a salary increase."

    After submitting your scenario, you will be presented with an overview of:

    • What the conversation will be about
    • What will make the conversation successful
    • Who the conversation is with (i.e., a short bio of your AI chat partner)

  3. Click Start to begin your role play

    • (Optional) If you would like to make change to your scenario, click Edit to manually define the scenario's goals, success criteria, and the AI's personality.

  4. Listen to your AI chat partner (captions available) and prepare a response. You can speak your response or type it into the chat.

  5. Continue the back and forth conversation.

  6. When the conversation reaches a natural conclusion, click End session. The personalized results page will offer feedback to help you close skill gaps.

docs.title: Mark a job as your Top Choice
Overview
docs.text:
While applying for a job with Easy Apply, Premium subscribers can mark the job as a Top Choice job. Top Choice job applications are more likely to stand out to hirers or recruiters.

Note

You can only mark up to three jobs as top choice job in a month.

  1. Begin an application with Easy Apply.

  2. During the application process, from the Mark this job as a top choice (Optional) section, select the checkbox to Mark job as a top choice.

  3. (Optional) Under Include a message with your application, you can type a statement describing why this job is a top choice.

  4. Submit your job application once all other fields are complete.

After you submit your application, the job lister can see that you marked their listing as a Top Choice job.

docs.title: See who has viewed your profile
Overview
docs.text:
Premium users can see who has viewed their profile (up to 365 days of history) as well as profile view trends. Profile view trends can indicate how well your profile attracts recruiters for the roles that interest you.

  1. On your profile page under the Analytics section, click Discover who's viewed your profile. This will open a new page.

  2. Under Who's viewed your profile, select a filter to sort recent viewers by recency, company, location, and more.

docs.title: Related tasks
docs.text: • Set up your profile

docs.title: View analytics for a job posting
Assess job match level
docs.text:
You can use Premium to assess how well your profile's qualifications match with a job listing's requirements.

  1. After finding a job listing, scroll down to find the job match prompt:

  2. Select an action to learn more about your match details. An AI-powered chat opens, detailing how your qualifications align with the job listing and providing further advice on interview preparation and expectations.

    You can continue to ask questions in the chat to learn more about the job match.

Info

Job match details are based on the qualifications you have listed in your LinkedIn profile. If you think that your match analysis does not accurately reflect your qualifications, try adding more experiences to your profile.

docs.title: Compare yourself with other applicants
docs.text: Scroll further down in the job listing to view data about other users who have applied for the job. This data includes total number of applicants, seniority, and education levels.

docs.title: View a company's hiring trends
docs.text:
Below applicant data, you can view summaries and visualizations of a company's hiring trends.

Interact with graphs and linked resources to learn more about any data point.

Note

The analytics provided by Premium are based on LinkedIn user data. They do not account for external applications or recruiting patterns.

docs.title: Profile sections
docs.text:
Profile sections allow you to display your professional experiences, education, skills, volunteer work, awards, and more to your colleagues. This information is only viewable from your full profile.

All profile sections are optional; however, certain sections (Core and Recommended) should be filled for greater visibility and credibility.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Although the standard (free) LinkedIn experience offers many tools to enhance your job search experience, Premium Career may be a better option for active job seekers who want an advantage over other applicants and direct access to recruiters.

See the comparisons below to decide which plan is right for you.

docs.title: Price
docs.text: Standard ($0) vs. Premium Career ($39.99/mo or ~$29.99/mo billed annually)

docs.title: Messaging & networking
docs.text: Feature Free Premium Career Message 1st-degree connections ✓ ✓ InMail credits (message anyone) ✗ 5/mo Open profile (receive free InMails) ✗ ✓ See who viewed your profile Last 5 viewers Full list

docs.text:

Note

Prices may vary by region and are subject to change, and LinkedIn periodically offers promotional free trials to its standard users. Verify current pricing on LinkedIn's official website before subscribing.
